reason: I have years of IrfanView set up with plug-ins, shortcuts and batch settings, and one developer's 0.4.1 doesn't beat that on trust alone. I'd install it for the cbz/zip reading and the gallery, but IrfanView stays the default.
why_switch_or_not: The things that interest me are the cbz/zip/7z support, the gallery with batch rename/convert, and the editor in one app, since I like one tool that views, edits and converts. But I won't make it my default for a month without a way to check it against my own huge folders and archives. There is no plug-in system and no community, so if something breaks on one of my odd files I have nobody to ask but one person.
current_app_pros: IrfanView is tiny and I know every shortcut. My plug-ins are set up, the batch convert/rename is dependable, and it handles my screenshots and PNG exports without fuss. It has been stable for years.
current_app_pains: Flipping fast through hundreds of screenshots can lag a bit. The interface looks dated, and the thumbnail browser is mediocre for big folders. I also have to hunt for plug-ins to cover newer formats.
objection: No plugins, no big community, hard to find help. It's one developer on version 0.4.1, and I don't know if it will still be maintained in two years or if it copes with my giant archive folders.
would_change_my_mind: I'd switch if it read my large cbz and zip collections quickly without choking and kept IrfanView-style batch conversion and shortcuts. It would also need some sign of lasting community or a public bug tracker with active replies.
